article.headline: Celtic Aim for Top Spot as Motherwell Stretches Squad Depth Amid Injuries
article.summary: Celtic faces Motherwell in a Scottish Premiership match at 12pm, with the visitors looking to reclaim the league lead.
article.body:
Motherwell manager Alfred Johansson confirmed his side will face Celtic without defender Dylan Williams, who is sidelined for several weeks following a hamstring injury. The squad also continues to manage the return of midfielder Regan Charles-Cook, who will not be available for this fixture after being placed on a specific return-to-play programme. Despite these absences, Johansson reported that all players who participated in the September international break have returned to the club in perfect health.

For Celtic, the match carries significant weight regarding their position in the Scottish Premiership standings. A victory over Motherwell would propel the Hoops back to the top of the league table. Manager Martin O'Neill enters the contest under pressure following a challenging run of form leading into the international break, making the result critical for the team's standing in the early stages of the campaign.

Motherwell’s preparations come off the back of a busy international window, which saw goalkeeper Alex Paulsen log significant minutes for New Zealand, including a clean sheet against China and a penalty shootout performance against Panama. While several Motherwell players gain match fitness through these international appearances, the team must now adjust its lineup to accommodate the recent injuries sustained during training.

The match is scheduled for a 12pm kick-off and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports. Both clubs look to stabilize their form as they navigate this upcoming sequence of matches in the Premiership.

article.headline: Police car mounts Geylang Bahru kerb and crashes into metal road barrier
article.summary: A 31-year-old police officer is assisting with investigations after his patrol vehicle hit a road divider on October 10.
article.body:
The front of the police vehicle suffered visible damage after mounting a kerb and colliding with a green barrier on Geylang Bahru Road, sending railings tumbling into the rightmost lane of traffic. The accident occurred at approximately 7:45 am while the vehicle was traveling toward Bendemeer Road, leaving the divider structure damaged at the scene.

This incident is currently under investigation by authorities, who confirmed that the 31-year-old male officer behind the wheel is assisting with those inquiries. While the vehicle collision disrupted the immediate area, local authorities stated that no injuries resulted from the impact. The aftermath of the crash was captured in footage circulating on social media, which shows the damaged cruiser alongside fallen road railings while other police personnel managed the site.

As investigations continue, the exact circumstances leading to the vehicle mounting the kerb remain undetermined. Witnesses who drove past the site noted the presence of multiple police officers securing the area and a secondary police car positioned across the roadway to manage the flow of traffic following the impact. There is no timeline provided for when the official findings of the investigation will be released or when the damaged road infrastructure will be fully repaired.

news.title: CJP Agitation Day 2: Left Student Groups Stage Flash Protest at Connaught Place, Detained by Police - India Today
news.og_title: CJP Agitation Day 2: Left Student Groups Stage Flash Protest at Connaught Place, Detained by Police
news.og_desc: A surprise protest broke out in New Delhi's Connaught Place on day two of the Cockroach Janta Party agitation, as left-leaning student groups, including AISA, AISF, and SFI, gathered unexpectedly near the inner circle. The demonstrators attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar via Janpath Road, raising slogans and demanding resignations to safeguard democracy. In response, Delhi Police and Rapid Action Force personnel deployed anti-riot gear, forming a human shield and barricading key lanes before detaining sixty to seventy protesters. Security forces maintained a heavy presence across Connaught Place, carrying out flag marches following market closures advised earlier by the New Delhi Traders Association. Correspondents reported that demonstrators used operational metro stations to stage flash gatherings after Jantar Mantar remained inaccessible due to heavy security arrangements.
